newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish prisoner 'executed' by fellow inmates.
newsitem.headline: Turkish prisoner 'executed' by fellow inmates.

text.p: A Turkish prisoner was killed on Wednesday by fellow inmates on orders of an outlawed far-left party for alleged collaboration with the authorities, Anatolian news agency reported.

Ibrahim Sertel, jailed for membership of the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party/Front (DHKP/C) in the western province of Izmir, was strangled and stabbed by two cellmates on the party's orders. He was 26.
His body, which had nearly 30 stab wounds, was found wrapped in a blanket and left by the door of the cell, the state-run agency said.
"Punished for working with the state," read a notice hung around the victim's neck, Anatolian said.
Another leftist prisoner was murdered on Tuesday by fellow inmates after a similar "execution" order by the DHKP/C against her and her sister for collaborating with the authorities.
The surviving sister, who was held in a separate prison, was later placed under strict security.
Prisons in Turkey are often denounced by politicians as training centres for "terrorists" and such disturbances have been a problem for successive governments.
Turkey's new Islamist-led goverment was hit by a domestic crisis in July when 12 people died as part of a hunger strike by 300 leftist prisoners in protest against jail conditions and alleged abuse.
